specification.problem: Tulsi-type quantum search on N=2^n items with one marked item w and one control (auxiliary) qubit, modified by projective Z-basis measurement of the control every tau iterations; study success probability P(w), control-search correlations, and the scaling of the optimal iteration count k* with N.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful instance: n=3 search qubits (N=8) plus 1 control qubit (4 qubits total), marked item w fixed, a free fixed angle theta, tau in {1,2,3,none}. Density-matrix (outcome-averaged) or trajectory simulation of k iterations; the n=3..8 scaling fit, MI and CCM computation are described but the exact paper definitions and angle choice are outside the scope.

symbols.meaning: angular parameter of the control rotation (free, replaces the standard N-dependent choice)
number of iterations between control measurements
symbols.domain: positive integer, or infinity for no measurement

symbols.meaning: probability of measuring w on the search register after k iterations
mutual information between search register S and control C

equations.label: Initial state
equations.description: Uniform superposition on search register; control starts in |+> (|0> is the alternative).
equations.justification: Sketch suggests |+> or |0>; the choice is not given in the abstract.
assumptions: Control initial state |+> chosen for the smallest instance

equations.label: Controlled iterate (proposed form)
equations.description: One step: oracle phase flip on w applied only when control is |1> (a single query per step), a control rotation Ry(theta), then Grover diffusion on the search register. This is a simplified stand-in for Tulsi's exact construction.
equations.justification: The abstract only says Tulsi's algorithm is modified with a different angular parameter; the precise Tulsi operators are not given, so this is a proposed construction.
assumptions: Diffusion acts on the search register only
Gate order and the exact role of theta are guesses

equations.label: Measured evolution
equations.description: Control dephasing in the Z basis every tau steps without reset; outcome-averaged state.
equations.justification: Intermediate control measurements with time lapse tau are stated; the no-reset, outcome-averaged form is an assumed implementation.

equations.label: Success probability
equations.description: Probability of reading the marked item from the search register.

equations.label: Mutual information
equations.description: Correlation between search and control registers, computed from reduced density matrices.
equations.justification: The abstract names Mutual Information; this is the standard definition. The Cumulative Correlation Measure definition is not given and is not reproduced here.

equations.label: Order estimate
equations.description: Empirical order: linear fit of log k* against log N over n=3..8. Expected alpha near 1/2 without measurement and near 1 for tau=1.
equations.abstract_quote: became of order $O(N)$ (classical brute force search) when the measurement is taken in every step
equations.justification: The abstract states O(N) when measuring every step; the fit procedure is an assumed way to estimate the order.

registers.name: S
registers.role: search register, qubit i holds bit i of x (little-endian), x=sum_i x_i 2^i

registers.name: C
registers.role: control/auxiliary qubit, measured in Z every tau steps

steps.description: Prepare H on all S qubits and the control in |+>.
Repeat for k=1..K: apply G_theta (one oracle query per iteration); after every tau-th iteration measure C in Z (dephase or sample a trajectory, no reset).
Record P_k(w) at each k for each tau and the no-measurement case; compute I(S:C) from the reduced states.
For n=3..8 find k* per tau and fit alpha.

specification.measurement: Final Z measurement of the n search qubits (counts, bits reversed per Qiskit little-endian) to estimate P(w); the control is measured mid-circuit only at multiples of tau. For statevector or density-matrix analysis, use the averaged state instead of counts.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Histogram frequency of w gives P(w); argmax over k gives k*; least-squares fit of log k* vs log N gives alpha; MI from the reduced density matrices.
assumptions: Control is the auxiliary qubit, Z-measured, not reset
Phase oracle controlled on control qubit
theta is a fixed free parameter, value not given
Small instance n=3 as the smallest construction
missing_information: Exact Tulsi operators and the standard angular parameter
The paper's specific alternative choice of theta
Tested values of tau and the range of k
Whether the measurement outcome is reset or kept
